'''Jill Whelan''' (born September 29, 1966)<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebrity birthdays for the week of Sept. 26-Oct. 2 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/olivia-newtonjohn-anne-robinson-linda-hamilton-bryan-ferry-jim-caviezel-b1923352.html |website=Independent |date=September 20, 2021 |publisher=via AP Newswire |access-date=2 July 2022}}</ref>  is an American actress. After working in television commercials, she landed her breakthrough role playing Vicki Stubing, the daughter of Captain Stubing, in six of the nine seasons of the American television series ''[[The Love Boat]]'' (1977–1986). She later guest starred on the revival ''[[Love Boat: The Next Wave]]''. She has had numerous guest roles in TV shows and played Lisa Davis in ''[[Airplane!]]'' In 2015, she was hired as a celebrations ambassador by Princess Cruises.

== Early life ==
Jill Whelan was born in [[Oakland, California]]. After auditioning and appearing in a local production of ''[[The King and I]]'' at the age of 8, she sent her school picture to a San Francisco Talent Agency and landed a series of TV commercials.<ref name="Huang">{{Cite web|url=https://rymanarts.org/news/meet-jill-whelan-host-ryman-arts-25th-anniversary-celebration|title=Meet Jill Whelan – host of Ryman Arts' 25th Anniversary Celebration!|last=Huang|first=Shannon|date=April 7, 2015|website=Ryman Arts|access-date=April 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220228013620/https://rymanarts.org/news/meet-jill-whelan-host-ryman-arts-25th-anniversary-celebration |archive-date=February 28, 2022}}</ref>

An M&M commercial<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inquisitr.com/2690363/love-boat-child-star-broke-jill-whelan-seeking-support-from-estranged-husband/|title='Love Boat' Child Star Broke: Jill Whelan Seeking Support From Estranged Husband|last=Dodrill|first=Tara|date=January 8, 2016|website=www.inquistr.com|access-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref> got her noticed by producers, and she was cast in [[Friends (1979 TV series)|''Friends'' (1979)]], which was quickly cancelled.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Single Season Sitcoms, 1948–1979: A Complete Guide|last=Leszczak|first=Robert|publisher=Mc Farland & Co Inc|year=2012|isbn=978-0-7864-6812-6|location=Jefferson, North Carolina|pages=52}}</ref> Concurrently, at the age of 11, she was cast as Vicki, daughter of ''The Love Boat's'' Captain Stubing. She initially appeared on the show as a guest star, and later became a series regular.

In 1984, Whelan graduated from the [[Buckley School (California)|Buckley School]] in [[Sherman Oaks]], California<ref>{{Cite news|last=Oates|first=Marie-Louise|date=November 3, 1982|title=Buckley School: A 50 Year Update|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/8336545/the_los_angeles_times/|journal=The Los Angeles Times|pages=104}}</ref> with a stint at [[Guildford College]] in [[Surrey]], England where she studied English Literature<ref name="Huang" /> before coming back to Los Angeles.

== Career ==
As well as starring in ''The Love Boat'', Whelan made numerous guest appearances in TV shows including ''[[Fantasy Island]]'' (twice), ''[[Vegas (1978 TV series)|Vegas]]'', ''[[Trapper John, M.D.]]'', ''[[Matt Houston]]'' and ''[[Battle of the Network Stars]]''. She also made guest appearances on game shows including ''[[Family Feud]]'', ''[[Body Language (game show)|Body Language]]'' and ''[[Password Plus and Super Password|Super Password]]''. In the 1980 disaster comedy film ''[[Airplane!]]'', Whelan played the role of Lisa Davis, a heart transplant patient.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Film Actors Guide|last=Lukanic|first=Steven A|publisher=Lone Eagle|year=1991|isbn=978-0-943728-38-4|pages=417}}</ref>

In the mid-1980s, in Los Angeles, having returned from England and with ''The Love Boat'' coming to an end, Whelan moved to New York City and worked as an event producer at [[Madison Square Garden]],<ref>{{Cite book|title=Prime-time hits: television's most popular network programs, 1950 to the present|last=Sackett|first=Susan|publisher=Bpi Communications|year=1993|isbn=978-0-8230-8392-3}}</ref> where she helped set up acts.

In 1999, Whelan left acting, started working as an investigative producer at the Los Angeles television station [[KCOP-TV]], and later became a radio show host for ''Talk Radio 1210 [[WPHT]]'' in Philadelphia.

On November 25, 2001, Whelan appeared on an episode of ''[[The Weakest Link]]'', a trivia game show hosted by [[Anne Robinson]]. Whelan competed against other celebrity 1970s TV stars, including [[Mackenzie Phillips]], [[Nell Carter]], [[Cindy Williams]], [[Joan Van Ark]], [[Erin Moran]], [[Erik Estrada]], and [[Fred Berry|Fred "Re-run" Berry]]. She outlasted the others, winning $57,000 for her charity.

On September 10, 2008, Whelan appeared with several other cast members from the movie ''[[Airplane!]]'' in a reunion segment on [[Today (NBC program)|NBC's ''Today Show'']]. In October 2008, she made her New York City cabaret debut with her one-woman show ''Jill Whelan: An Evening in Dry Dock'' at the Metropolitan Room.<ref>{{cite web|last=BWW News Desk|title=THE LOVE BOAT and AIRPLANE'S Jill Whelan Begins at Metropolitan Room Oct. 6|url=http://www.broadwayworld.com/article/THE-LOVE-BOAT-and-AIRPLANES-Jill-Whelan-Begins-at-Metropolitan-Room-Oct-6-20081005#|publisher=BroadwayWorld.com|access-date=January 13, 2014}}</ref> From September to November 2011, Whelan appeared in the British farce ''Move Over Mrs. Markham'' at Stage West Theatre Restaurant in the Toronto, Ontario area.

Whelan was set to replace [[Mark Thompson (radio)|Mark Thompson]], who retired on August 17, 2012, after 25 years co-hosting ''[[The Mark & Brian Show]]'' on [[KLOS]] in Los Angeles, but during Thompson's final broadcast, co-host [[Brian Phelps]] announced that he, too, was quitting KLOS.

In 2013, Whelan became co-host with Brian Phelps of ''The Brian and Jill Show''. The two share a love for improvisational comedy, and have created hundreds of characters together that they have performed on stage during improvisation shows and in sketches on their podcast.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2012/09/27/when-jill-whelan-met-brian-phelps-it-was-instant-chemistry/|title=When Jill Whelan met Brian Phelps, it was 'instant chemistry'|last=Lycan|first=Gary|date=September 27, 2012|website=Orange County Register|access-date=April 1, 2019}}</ref>

Whelan is mentioned in "Dead Man Sliding", the tenth episode of the third season of ''[[Sliders (TV series)|Sliders]]'', as an actress who never had relevance in the dimension of the protagonists.

== Personal life ==
During the early 1980s, Whelan served as a national spokeswoman for [[First Lady of the United States|First Lady]] [[Nancy Reagan]]'s "[[Just Say No]]" anti-drug campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biography.com/news/the-love-boat-cast-where-are-they-now|title='The Love Boat' Cast: Where Are They Now?|last=Ulster|first=Laurie|date=November 23, 2014|website=Biography|access-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref>

Whelan met her first husband, Brad St. John, as an associate producer for KCOP-TV in Los Angeles, shortly after leaving Madison Square Garden. They married in December 1993. Soon after their wedding, she became pregnant with her first son, Harrison. Whelan divorced St. John in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Jennifer Wulff |date=June 11, 2001| access-date=May 31, 2021 | title=Beyond the Sea |url=https://people.com/archive/beyond-the-sea-vol-55-no-23/ |work=[[People (magazine)|People]] 55/2001|quote= At the same time she is going through a painful divorce from businessman Brad St. John—the father of her son Harrison, 6, and the man she blames for the loss of her Love Boat savings.}}</ref>

Returning to the East Coast, she married her second husband, Michael Chaykowsky, in April 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Archive – Passages|url=https://people.com/archive/passages-vol-61-no-15/|last=L. Redwood|first=Tina|date=April 19, 2004|website=PEOPLE.com|language=EN|access-date=May 28, 2020}}</ref> Her second son, Grant, was born in 2006.  In 2014, Whelan filed for divorce from Chaykowsky.<ref name="Divorce2">{{cite news|url=https://www.tmz.com/2014/06/26/love-boat-star-jill-whelan-airplane-divorce/#ixzz35s65HAXm|title= 'Love Boat' Star Marriage Capsizes |date=June 26, 2014|work=TMZ|access-date=May 31, 2021}}</ref>

In 2015, Whelan was hired by Princess Cruises as  a celebrations ambassador.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ftnnews.com/cruise-travel/27133-jill-whelan-to-represent-princess-cruises-celebrations.html|title=Jill Whelan to represent Princess Cruises' celebrations|last=Tore|first=Ozgur|date=May 7, 2015|website=FTN News|access-date=April 1, 2019}}</ref>

Whelan married former [[Denver Broncos]] quarterback [[Jeff Knapple]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.amomama.com/189154-the-love-boat-jill-whelan-met-her-third.html|title='The Love Boat' Jill Whelan Met Her Third Husband through Her High School Prom Date|last=Rivas|first=Aby|date=January 18, 2020|website=Amo Mama|access-date=February 23, 2021}}</ref>
